title: Breaking overwhelming tasks into smaller pieces
content: When everything feels like too much at once, a long mental list of responsibilities can itself become a major source of stress. Try picking just one task and breaking it into the smallest possible first step - not 'finish the project' but 'open the document and write one sentence.' Completing even a tiny step can create a sense of momentum and control, which often matters more for reducing stress than how much actually gets finished.

title: Short movement breaks to release physical tension
content: Stress tends to build up in the body as muscle tension, especially in the shoulders, neck, and jaw. A short break to physically move - even just a 5-minute walk, some stretching, or shaking out your arms and shoulders - can help release that built-up tension. This isn't about exercise for fitness, just giving the body a chance to reset before going back to whatever is causing the stress.

title: Setting boundaries when overcommitted
content: A common source of ongoing stress is taking on more than there's realistically time or energy for, often out of guilt or fear of disappointing others. It can help to practice a simple, honest way of declining or renegotiating commitments - something like 'I want to help, but I can't take this on right now without it affecting my other responsibilities.' Protecting time and energy isn't selfish; it's often what allows someone to actually follow through well on the commitments they do keep.

title: When stress may be turning into burnout
content: Everyday stress is normal, but it's worth paying attention if stress becomes constant rather than tied to specific events, or comes with exhaustion that doesn't improve with rest, irritability, trouble concentrating, or a sense of feeling detached from things that used to matter. These can be signs of burnout, which often benefits from more than just personal coping strategies - talking to a doctor, therapist, or even reassessing workload with a manager or mentor can make a real difference.
